facts.text: I have a student who gets the A-frame in agility correct 95% of the time.
I have a student who gets the dogwalk in agility correct 95% of the time.
I have a student who gets the teeter in agility correct 95% of the time.
I have a student who gets the weaves in agility correct 95% of the time.
I have a student who gets the backsides in agility correct 95% of the time.
I have a student who keeps all the bars up in agility 95% of the time.
I have a course with 1 A-frame, 1 dogwalk, 1 teeter, 1 weaves, and 2 backsides.
I asked for the chance that the student runs without making a mistake.
I asked to include the 95% chance that the student keeps up all the bars.
I stated that the chance the student makes at least one mistake is about 30% and asked if that is correct.
I asked for the chances that the student makes at least one mistake in 4 consecutive runs.
I stated that the chance of not making any mistake is 70% and asked for the chances of running 4 consecutive runs without making any mistakes.
I asked for the chances of not making any mistakes over 10 runs.
